name: Send newsletters and automated email flows
summary: Writes and schedules newsletters, and starts or pauses automated email flows, in the business's own email platform. Crons read, draft and queue; a person approves every scheduled send and every flow change.

all.evidence: 31 of the 40 email marketing calls describe how they run it

covered_by.list-building: gap (lists come from property and lead platforms that are not mapped)
covered_by.write-copy: draft (the agent writes the newsletter into the store; the draft cron creates the campaign)
covered_by.approve: approval (every scheduled send and flow change waits in the CRM shell)
covered_by.schedule-send: approval (Mailchimp schedule, after the draft is in place)
covered_by.automation-build: approval (start or pause a flow email); writing flow email content is a gap
covered_by.track-results: sync (open and click rates against the owner's targets)
covered_by.follow-up-replies: skill (replies are read and drafted by the agent; no reply operation is mapped)

crons.name: sync
crons.summary: Read recent campaign results and each platform's flows. Flag sends under the owner's targets. Changes nothing.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Create a Mailchimp draft campaign for each newsletter the agent has written, then queue its scheduled send for approval.

crons.name: flows
crons.summary: Queue each flow start, pause, live or manual change the agent has proposed, for approval.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads, a campaign saved in Mailchimp's draft state, and its content. Anything that schedules, sends, starts or pauses an email, or changes a flow's status, is a live operation and waits for a person.

mailchimp.covers: newsletter as a draft campaign, schedule for approval, reports, automated email start and pause for approval

klaviyo.covers: flow list, and flow live or manual change for approval

gaps: Klaviyo newsletters: creating a campaign needs its message details (subject, sender, template) mapped first; only flows are drafted and changed for Klaviyo.
Klaviyo results: query_campaign_values is a POST that the kit marks as a write, so the cron cannot read Klaviyo open and click rates until the kit reads it as a read.
ActiveCampaign: its pages are blog articles only (status docs-read); it has no adapter. Build it after a sandbox account is confirmed.
HubSpot record-keeping, list building from property or lead platforms (ID4Me and similar), and reply handling are not mapped; they stay with the owner or the agent skill.
Writing automated flow email content (the email body, not its status) is not mapped for Mailchimp or Klaviyo here; flow copy is written in the platform by a person.
Mailchimp schedule_time format and whether a campaign passes the send checklist are unconfirmed on a live account; confirm on a Mailchimp test account before the first approval.
Mailchimp and Klaviyo are status spec: offline tests only. Neither adapter has run against a real account.
core/capabilities.json has no campaign create or schedule capability; the capabilities above are the nearest existing names.

tools/deploy.ts reads only the quoting keys from settings (intake, quotes, rate_card, messages), so a deploy of this workflow would render no secret names until secretNames covers platforms; that is a core change.

There is no CLI command to write a newsletter or flow proposal into the store; the agent (or the CRM shell) must write them to the newsletters and flow-changes namespaces until a propose command exists.

evidence.calls: 40 email marketing calls read, 31 describe the process; schedule-send, automation-build, approval, tracking and follow-up are 88 to 100 percent manual, write-copy 33 percent
evidence.platforms: Mailchimp and Klaviyo mapped step by step from their official specs in the endpoint map; ActiveCampaign from its help articles only
